question: Should the draft Claws contract allow a package to claim globally named MCP servers in shared OpenClaw configuration and remove them later when their digest remains unchanged?
rationale: The patch establishes an executable configuration, persistence, export, and cleanup ownership contract that the still-open RFC explicitly has not finalized.

options.title: Approve guarded ownership
options.body: Accept global MCP ownership only with complete consent, deterministic pending-state recovery, collision rejection, digest drift checks, and compare-before-unset cleanup.

options.title: Keep MCP advisory
options.body: Allow manifests, status, and export to describe MCP servers while requiring operators to perform shared configuration changes manually.

options.title: Defer MCP lifecycle
options.body: Keep MCP actions unsupported until the RFC defines a narrower scoped ownership model.

recommendation.title: Approve guarded ownership
recommendation.body: Accept global MCP ownership only with complete consent, deterministic pending-state recovery, collision rejection, digest drift checks, and compare-before-unset cleanup.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest current-main owner signal for the shared MCP configuration writer and its mutation contract.
